correctness.rationale: For binary \(3\times n\) matrices with no isolates and exactly \(n+2\) links, column degree excess is two, admitting only one degree-three column or two degree-two columns. Case I contributes \(n-1\) from columns and at most \(5/2\) from rows; case II with distinct two-column neighborhoods contributes at most \(2(n-2)\) from columns and two from rows, attaining equality only when all singleton columns select the common row; identical degree-two neighborhoods yield a strict gap because the third row cannot be isolated. This proves the bound and unique form for every \(n\ge4\), gives 3n(n-1) labeled extrema, and exactly evaluates the Ferrers comparator. Two unrelated exact rational scoring methods agree on each of 63,906 admissible matrices at sizes \(n=2,\dots,7\), with the expected first-layer equality classification.

evidence: Almeida-Neto et al. (2008) introduce NODF, emphasizing decreasing marginal totals and overlap but not the fixed-link 3-by-n optimum.
Britton et al. (2015) prove exact characterizations for NODF equal to 0 or 1 and analyze its metric, not this constrained maximum.
Song et al. (2017) discuss the maximum NODF attainable given dimensions and links and use a greedy link-addition algorithm instead of a sharp analytic formula.

Hoeppke and Simmons (2021) explicitly say fixed-size/fixed-link NODF maximization is nonconvex and describe greedy, hill-climbing and simulated-annealing algorithms that do not certify global optimum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources frame and partially cover the same ecological optimization task, but none provides an exact universal sparse three-row formula or equality classification. A general numerical optimization algorithm cannot logically imply the stated closed-form sharp bound and uniqueness without a proof of global optimality.

originality.rationale: The definition and perfect-nestedness matrix characterizations are known; recent ecological literature specifically asks for maximum NODF at fixed network size and number of interactions but provides heuristic optimizations. No searched primary source or indexed record states the exact three-row minimal-connected-link extremum, the forced non-Ferrers equality shape, or the universal labeled enumeration. The older unrestricted-link extremum is not stronger in this fixed-link subdomain: it allows its optimum to use additional links and has Ferrers rather than non-Ferrers maximizers.

value.rationale: Fixed-size/fixed-link maximum NODF is used to normalize ecological nestedness comparisons, and published heuristics do not furnish a certificate of global optimality. The exact \((2n-2)/K\) bound provides a sharp calibration over a natural minimal-connected-link regime at all \(n\ge4\). The complete equality classification reveals a structural paradox: optimization of the conventional nestedness score forces two specialist species to use incomparable partner sets, while the best truly Ferrers matrix loses \((n-3)/K\). This gives a meaningful mathematical boundary on the interpretation of NODF, not a routine recomputation of a known nested matrix.
